failed_checks.name: appearance
failed_checks.reason: Native render reads as soft, short plush fur, but the exported representation shows conspicuous portable-coat artifacts: sparse, dark dot/card speckling across the white and black regions plus many short spike-like tufts sticking out along the silhouette (head, torso, limbs), giving a “prickly/porcupine” look rather than neatly groomed short fur. There is also a small ridge/tuft cluster on top of the head visible in both native and exported that looks like an unintended groom lump rather than tidy plush fur. Dragon remains distinct and not covered in panda fur, but overall exported coat look violates the requested neat short-fur appearance.

failed_checks.name: deformation
failed_checks.reason: During the toy_dance pose sample (notably around the provided isolated frame), the torso/belly shows a strong, sharp fold/crease and surface shearing that reads as deformation rather than plush squash. The exported isolated pose in particular shows the white belly region and torso silhouette warping with visible creasing while the portable coat accentuates the distortion, which counts as major deformation for this stylized plush character.

checks.name: framing
checks.reason: Full-body panda and perched shoulder dragon are visible in front/side/back/three-quarter views for both native and exported, and the motion contact sheet keeps the character in frame without added props/clothing/scenery.

checks.name: deformation
checks.reason: Sampled motion frames and the isolated “greatest recorded edge stretch” pose do not show a clear catastrophic collapse/tearing; proportions stay coherent through the dance poses in both native and exported snapshots. Numeric deformation gate reports no severe spike failure for the sampled poses (not a full visual guarantee).

limitations: Motion review is based on the provided contact sheet and isolated pose snapshots; it does not prove all frames are collision-free or physically plausible. (evidence-motion-00, evidence-isolated-native-toy_dance, evidence-isolated-exported-toy_dance)
Return-to-start and deformation assessments are sampled/endpoint-based per the provided numeric proofs, not a certified seamless loop or full-frame deformation audit. (action-audit-toy_dance)

(evidence-exported-views, evidence-motion-00)

Adjust the toy_dance animation so the “small whole-body hops” are visibly readable (clear up-and-down body motion, not just side leans/sways), while keeping the dragon perched/attached and ending in the starting pose. (evidence-motion-00)

state_reviews.reason: The clip reads as a gentle side-to-side toy sway with head tilts and some arm movement, and the dragon stays perched/attached. However the required “small whole-body hops” are not clearly readable in the provided motion frames (feet/body do not visibly hop; motion reads primarily as leaning/swaying). Geometry does change over time (not constant), and endpoint return is supported by the audit.

requirement_reviews.reason: The motion frames show alternating side-to-side beats across the 4 seconds, and the audit reports rhythmic reversals consistent with a three-beat pattern.

Side-to-side sway is visible, but the requested small whole-body hops are not clearly readable in the provided frames (no obvious hop/airtime or distinct up-down beat accent apparent). Audit travel/vertical rise alone is not sufficient to establish visually readable hops.
Arms show coordinated motion with the beats (subtle but visible changes in arm positions across sampled frames), consistent with toy-style arm swings.
Head tilt/rotation is visibly present across the beat frames, reading as gentle toy-like tilts.
Dragon remains perched on the shoulder throughout the shown frames with no separation or flight; it follows the body/shoulder motion as required.
End pose appears to return to the start in the motion sheet, and the audit reports low endpoint displacement for the body.
Arms appear back in the starting/rest position at clip end; audit supports endpoint return within threshold.
Head returns to a neutral/starting orientation by the end frame set; audit supports endpoint return within threshold.

review.summary: Identity, framing, and deformation are acceptable in the sampled evidence, and the dragon stays perched. Acceptance fails because (1) exported fur/coat quality does not match the requested soft, neatly groomed plush fur (visible stubbly/streaky coat artifacts), and (2) the toy_dance meaning requirement for readable small hops is not met from the provided motion frames.
